newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss Diax telecoms group eyes public share offer.
newsitem.headline: Swiss Diax telecoms group eyes public share offer.

text.p: The Diax telecommunications group, starting up to challenge Swiss Telecom when the market is liberalised next year, is studying whether to offer shares to the public eventually, chairman Hans-Peter Aebi said.
"This is a serious possibility," he told reporters, but added a final decision had not yet been made.

Officials said they planned to invest 500 million to 600 million Swiss francs to become a full-service provider in three to five years. It will employ up to 1,000 workers by the year 2001, excluding mobile phone operations for which it will also seek a license.

Diax Holding groups six Swiss electrical utilities -- Aare Tessin AG fr Elektrizitaet (Atel), Berner Kraftwerke, Centralschweizeriche Kraftwerke (CKW), Elektrizitaetsgesellschaft Laufenburg (ELG), L'Energie de L'Ouest-Suisse (EOS) und Nordostschweizerischen Kraftwerke (NOK) -- and Swiss Re.
Swiss Re is a passive investor whose double-digit million Swiss franc investment has given it a stake of around 25 to 30 percent, Aebi said.

Diax Holding owns 60 percent and SBC Communications Inc 40 percent of diAx, the group's telecoms operating company. It is this company that could seek a bourse listing, but only after around five years, board member Juerg Gassmann said

It expects to win a double-digit share of the 10 billion franc market, but officials were not more specific. The market is expected to grow four percent a year, said Werner Meier, deputy managing director.

SBC Europe chief Robert Shaner said Switzerland, as the world's 12th-largest market and with the second-highest number of telephone lines per capita, was an attractive market that fit in well with SBC's growth strategy.
Gassmann said fibre-optic cable would be laid this year along 1,700 km of of the 8,000 km of high-tension lines the group controlled.
